title: The showroom
about: The running case for the refresher (format/refresher.md section 4): the showroom givens, the course's own assumptions, and every figure each lesson works out, with its rule and inputs. Built by a script that works each figure from the inputs shown with it. Reshaped 20 Oct for the app (RUNBOOK section 8): a flat figures list, each naming its lesson and, for a Section A part, its part; figures still to be worked are in pending (see case.notes.md).
edition: BS 7671:2018+A2:2022, as Dan's course taught it (flowchart title). Whether A3:2024 changes anything here is not checked.
rounding: Each figure is worked from the inputs shown with it, rounded half up: currents, voltages, powers and kW to 2 decimal places, impedances to 3, CSA to 2, lengths to 1. A maximum is rounded down. A typed answer is accepted within "accept" where given (it covers √3 taken as 1.73, as slides p.13 do, and unrounded working).

scenario.title: Your showroom: the motor
scenario.text: A newly built car retailer; cars are driven over the showroom's concrete floor. Supply: three phase four wire 400 V, TN-C-S, Ze declared as 0.1 Ω, prospective fault current 4.6 kA; ambient 20 °C. Five boards: MDB, DBL1, DBL2, DBP1 and DBP2. In the consultation bay, a 400 V three-phase 11 kW motor, power factor 0.8 lagging, efficiency 86%, controlled by a star-delta starter and not subject to frequent starting and stopping. The cables from the starter to the motor are 90 °C thermosetting singles in conduit.
scenario.source: Your assignment ED4-01A: pack p.3, and question 4 on p.4.

assumptions.label: How the lighting current is worked from the key watts
assumptions.value: I = (tube watts x (1 + ballast loss)) / (230 V x power factor) for fluorescent fittings; (watts) / (230 V x power factor) for the others
assumptions.why: The Schneider guide says the tube power excludes the ballast and gives 25% and a power factor to use; an older book (Whitfield, sources 188, 189) instead multiplies discharge lighting by 1.8. The lesson uses the first and names the second.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: lighting current = key watts (plus the ballast loss for fluorescent fittings) / (230 V x power factor), using the practice values p.pf.fluo, p.ballast, p.pf.led and p.pf.other. An older book multiplies discharge lighting by 1.8 instead.

assumptions.label: Which luminaires DBL2 feeds
assumptions.why: Question 1b leaves the split to the designer (pack p.4). DBL2 is in the tools and warranty store, so it takes the rooms around it; DBL1, in the plant room, takes the west and north, the external column luminaires and the door bulkheads.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: DBL2 (tools and warranty store) feeds the east of the building: the consultation bay, the toilets, cleaner and tea bay, the two stores, the showroom east of the welcome desk, service reception, the foyer and the six walkway bollards: 55 LED 26 W, 18 modular 4 x 36 W, 4 twin 58 W and 6 bollards 18 W. DBL1 (plant room) feeds the rest: 103 LED, 16 modular, 12 twin, the 9 wall spots, the 6 columns and the 6 bulkheads.

assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: a "Twin 1700mm Fluo Luminaire 58W" holds two 58 W tubes, 116 W a fitting (the cautious reading; the key does not say).

assumptions.label: DBL2's lighting circuits and their phases

assumptions.why: Question 1b asks for the loads balanced across circuits (pack p.4); the circuits follow the rooms, and the phases are chosen to share the current about equally.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: DBL2 has seven lighting circuits. C1 consultation bay (6 modular); C2 uni-sex and female toilets (5 modular); C3 cleaner, male toilets and tea bay (7 modular); C4 tools and warranty store and oil store (4 twin); C5 showroom east of the welcome desk (28 LED); C6 service reception (21 LED); C7 foyer (6 LED) and the walkway bollards (6). L1: C1 and C5; L2: C3 and C6; L3: C2, C4 and C7.

assumptions.label: Socket circuits for maximum demand
assumptions.value: eight 32 A circuits, one per area
assumptions.why: The drawing does not give circuits (brief section 2); question 10 asks for informed assumptions (pack p.5).
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: the sockets are eight 32 A circuits, one per area: the trade parts counter; the parts manager and service and parts admin; Sales and the west desks; the other desks; Hospitality and parts sale with the ceiling-void sockets; the west floor boxes; the east floor boxes and welcome desk; the consultation bay, service reception, stores and plant room.

assumptions.label: Diversity on the lighting
assumptions.why: The showroom lights are on together from 7.30 am to 9 pm (pack p.4, question 5a), and the Schneider guide advises factors close to unity for mainly lighting circuits (research source 177). The On-Site Guide's small-shop column would allow 90%.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: no diversity on the lighting, because the showroom lights are on together through opening hours (question 5a). The On-Site Guide would allow 90% for a shop; a designer could take it.

assumptions.label: Spreading the single-phase loads for maximum demand
assumptions.why: An older book works a three-phase line current as the single-phase total divided by three when a perfect balance is assumed (research source 191). Real circuits do not share out exactly, so the heaviest phase will be a little higher.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: for the whole installation's maximum demand the single-phase loads are taken as shared evenly, so each phase carries their total ÷ 3, plus the motor's line current. An estimate: the heaviest phase will be a little higher.

assumptions.label: The motor circuit's device: type C, 25 A
assumptions.value: a type C circuit-breaker to BS EN 60898, 25 A, at DBP2
assumptions.why: In must not be less than Ib (23.08 A): 25 A is the smallest standard rating that is not (the rating columns of On-Site Guide Table B6, source 223). Type C trips instantaneously at 5 to 10 In (125 to 250 A at 25 A; On-Site Guide Table 7.2.7(ii), sources 220-222), clear of the practice star start (62.32 A) with room for the changeover surge; type B (75 to 125 A) clears it by little. The breaker gives short-circuit protection and back-up; the motor and the starter-to-motor cables are protected against overload by the starter's thermal relay (a thermal relay is not a device Regulation 433.1.201 covers, so its own characteristic is checked, source 243).
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: the motor circuit is protected at DBP2 by a type C circuit-breaker to BS EN 60898, 25 A: the smallest standard rating not below Ib (23.08 A). Type C trips instantaneously at 5 to 10 In (125 to 250 A), clear of the practice star start (62.32 A); the starter's thermal relay protects the motor and the starter-to-motor cables against overload.

assumptions.label: The overload relay is in the delta circuit, set at the winding current
assumptions.why: In the standard star-delta arrangement the thermal relay sits between the main contactor and the motor, carrying the winding current, so it is set at 0.58 × the motor In (Schneider Electric and Siemens, sources 225, 226; ElectroMechCalc, source 244). A relay in the incoming line is set at the full motor In instead (Schneider type 2 coordination), and the six starter-to-motor cables would still carry the winding current in delta running (source 227).
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: the starter's thermal overload relay sits in the delta circuit and is set at the winding current, 13.33 A (23.08 A ÷ √3, which is 0.58 × the motor's In). This is the "In" (current setting) of the protective device for the starter-to-motor cables.

assumptions.label: The starter-to-motor conduit is on a wall: Reference Method B
assumptions.value: surface conduit on the consultation bay wall, no thermal insulation (Ci = 1, Cf = 1)
assumptions.why: The pack says only "in conduit". Reference Method B is conduit on a wall or in trunking (Table 4E1A heading, source 216; IET Wiring Matters, source 239). If it ran in a thermally insulating wall (Reference Method A, column 3) 1.5 mm² still passes: 17 A against 16.66 A.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: the starter-to-motor conduit is surface mounted on the consultation bay's wall (Reference Method B), clear of thermal insulation, so Ci and Cf are 1. In a thermally insulating wall (Reference Method A) 1.5 mm² would still pass (17 A against 16.66 A).

assumptions.label: Six singles in one conduit are two three-phase circuits: Cg = 0.80
assumptions.value: Cg 0.80 (Table 4C1 item 1, two circuits, bunched and enclosed)
assumptions.why: In delta running every one of the six conductors carries the winding current (source 244), and Table 4C1 note 5 treats n single-core cables as n/3 circuits of three loaded conductors (sources 213, 219): six singles are two circuits, and bunched and enclosed two circuits give 0.80 (source 212). The three-phase column of Table 4E1A (3 or 4 loaded cables) is then used, not the two-cable column.
assumptions.text: The course's own assumption: the six singles from the starter to the motor, all loaded in delta running, are two three-phase circuits in one conduit: Table 4C1 item 1, two circuits, Cg = 0.80, read in Table 4E1A's column for 3 or 4 loaded cables.
